cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Bilingualism ≠ Monolingualism – the ability to speak two languages fluently.

p.em: Example: Early bilingualism enhances executive control networks.

cosy-blockquote.p: Neuroplasticity ≠ Rigidity – the ability of the brain to form and reorganize synaptic connections.

p.em: Example: Neuroplasticity allows the brain to adapt throughout adulthood.

cosy-blockquote.p: Cognitive Reserve ≠ Cognitive vulnerability – the brain's resilience to neuropathological damage.

p.em: Example: Language learning builds substantial cognitive reserve.

cosy-blockquote.p: Inhibition ≠ Impulsivity – the ability to suppress irrelevant responses or distractions.

p.em: Example: Bilinguals practice active inhibition when selecting words.

cosy-blockquote.p: Dementia ≠ Mental acuity – a chronic or persistent mental process disorder caused by brain disease.

p.em: Example: Bilingualism can delay dementia onset by several years.

cosy-blockquote.p: Executive Control ≠ Automatic response – higher-level cognitive processes managing goal-directed action.

p.em: Example: Executive control improves through constant task switching.

cosy-blockquote.p: Stimulus ≠ Sedative – a thing or event that evokes a specific functional reaction.

p.em: Example: Language immersion acts as a powerful cognitive stimulus.

cosy-blockquote.p: Adaptation ≠ Stagnation – the process of changing to better suit an environment.

p.em: Example: Brain adaptation occurs when learning complex grammar.

cosy-blockquote.p: Synapse ≠ Degeneration – a junction between two nerve cells.

p.em: Example: Strong synapses support fast memory recall.

cosy-blockquote.p: Longevity ≠ Short lifespan – long life or existence.

p.em: Example: Mental activity promotes brain health longevity.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
How does bilingualism stimulate neuroplasticity across different age groups?
★ When did you first notice your brain adapting to a second language?

Why does language switching strengthen executive control and active inhibition?
★ Do you ever accidentally insert words from another language when speaking?

How does building cognitive reserve help delay symptoms of dementia?
★ How do you keep your mind challenged in daily life?

Why is language immersion such an effective cognitive stimulus?
★ Have you ever experienced full language immersion?

How does structural brain adaptation support lifelong mental longevity?
★ What mental habits do you hope to maintain in old age?

★ Would you support government funding for adult language classes?

How might future brain imaging technology measure individual cognitive reserve in real time?
★ Would you like to see a digital scan of your own brain?

How does early inhibition practice benefit children in non-language school subjects?
★ How good are you at ignoring digital distractions while working?

What role will bilingualism play in future multicultural workplaces?
★ How often do you use multiple languages in your job or studies?
